brief: Goldman's US equities desk note (Tue 15 Sep close, ahead of Wednesday's FOMC decision) frames the day's modest equity decline (S&P -45bps to 7,585) as driven by oil and rates. WTI crude jumped 4.4% above $105/barrel on Saudi Arabia's Yanbu shipment suspensions, a Libya supply suspension, and Houthi attack momentum; the resulting energy-sector rally weighed on sentiment and the consumer space, producing poor breadth (344 S&P names down). The 10-year yield pushed back above 5% with the FOMC meeting tomorrow carrying above-90% hike odds and two hikes priced through year end. The AI trade stabilized as Nvidia's and Broadcom's CEOs pushed back on compute/capex slowdown concerns, though megacap tech stayed mostly lower (Amazon down 6 of 7 sessions). Desk activity was light (3/10) and better for sale; asset managers sold macro products, hedge funds were flat. At GS's Consumer Conference, "resilient" was the dominant word (Walmart, Visa/Mastercard), but the note argues investors doubt consumer health less than they doubt their own ability to profit being long consumer names, leaving a collective shrug.
